title: Zeroth hypercohomology preserves quasi-coherent coproducts on a qcqs algebraic space
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: every open cover of $|X|$ admits a finite subcover, and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact, i.e. the diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ of $X$ regarded as an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ through $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $C_X$ for its full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. For every small family $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ in $C_X$ and every coproduct cofan $\iota_i:E_i\to E$ in the ambient $D(\mathcal O_X)$, the canonical homomorphism
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}H^0(X,E_i)\longrightarrow H^0(X,E)$$
is bijective. Here $H^0(X,-)=H^0R\Gamma(X,-)$ is zeroth hypercohomology [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], and the map restricts on summand $i$ to $H^0(X,\iota_i)$. No common cohomological bound or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed; the empty family is included.

source.place: Tag 08FB, label lemma-quasi-coherence-pushforward-direct-sums; the global zeroth-hypercohomology consequence explicitly invoked in the first paragraph of proposition-compact-is-perfect.

proof.text: Set $F=\Gamma(X,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$. The small-site module category is Grothendieck abelian and admits K-injective resolutions. Abelian groups are $\mathbf Z$-modules, so their category is also Grothendieck abelian. Ambient coproducts are termwise sums of representatives, and $H^r(E)=\bigoplus_i H^r(E_i)$. Quasi-coherent modules are closed under sums, kernels and cokernels; thus $E$ and all good truncations in use have quasi-coherent cohomology. Exactness of sums also makes good truncations commute with sums: at the boundary degree compute the kernel or cokernel of the differential. These identifications preserve each coprojection, and apply to any specified coproduct cofan by its unique isomorphism with the termwise model. The formula $F(M)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_X,M)$ makes $F$ additive, left exact and product preserving: a map into a product is precisely a family of maps.

source.place: Tag 08F3, lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-sums; Tag 08FB, truncations and sums

proof.text: Choose a uniform bound for $F$ as follows. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and apply the change-of-base lemma with $S'=T$: $j_!X$ is an algebraic space over $T$ (part (1)), and by part (3) it has the same small etale site and structure sheaf as $X$, hence the same module sheaves, quasi-coherent modules, functor $F$ and derived functors $R^pF$. Its point space is $|X|$ (same atlases and field points, as in step 1 of the qcqs permanence lemma), so $j_!X$ is quasi-compact, and by the statement its diagonal over $T$ is quasi-compact. Work with $j_!X$, written $X$, over the base scheme $T$. The absolute diagonal of $T$ is the identity and $T$ is quasi-compact: a cover refines to basic opens $D(a)$, the covering elements generate the unit ideal, and an expression for $1$ uses finitely many of them. Thus $T$ is quasi-separated. The qcqs permanence lemma gives that $f:X\to T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the affine-chart uniform vanishing lemma to $Y=V=T$ and $\operatorname{id}_T:V\to Y$. Here $X\times_TV=X$, and evaluation of the extension $\widetilde M$ at $X$ is global sections of $M$: the enlarged-site equivalence identifies maps from the structure module with its sections at the terminal object $X$. Consequently that lemma gives one $N\geq1$ with $R^pF(M)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $M$ and $p\geq N$. Neither a dimension bound on $X$ nor a bound on the family has been introduced.

proof.text: For every $p\geq0$, $R^pF$ preserves sums of module sheaves. To apply the abelian-sheaf colimit theorem, use the enlarged etale site, where $X$ is terminal. Its equivalence with the small site preserves global sections, colimits and injectives: an additive equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels, and its inverse transports the injective extension property. Hence it identifies the derived evaluations as well. Apply the module-to-abelian evaluation comparison at $X$ there. Together with preservation of colimits by forgetting modules, the filtered-colimit theorem for abelian sheaf cohomology now gives the corresponding assertion for $R^pF$ on modules. Write a sum as the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, indexed by finite subsets of $I$, including the empty subset. Additivity of derived functors identifies the higher cohomology of a finite subsum with the finite sum of higher cohomologies. The resulting isomorphism $\bigoplus_iR^pF(M_i)\cong R^pF(\bigoplus_iM_i)$ has on each summand exactly the map induced by its coprojection.

source.place: Tag 08FB, last sentence; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 073E, lemma-colimits; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD

proof.text: First consider objects $K_i$ with a common lower cohomological bound $a$, and their ambient sum $K$ with injections $u_i$. Step 1 gives the same bound for $K$ and $H^r(K)=\bigoplus_iH^r(K_i)$. The natural single-object identification in the truncation spectral sequence is $H^p(RF(M[0]))\cong R^pF(M)$ for $p\geq0$. By step 3 every canonical comparison $\bigoplus_i H^p(RF(H^r(K_i)[0]))\to H^p(RF(H^r(K)[0]))$ is therefore an isomorphism. Apply the bounded-below coproduct filtration lemma with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ab}$, $F=\Gamma(X,-)$ and total degree $0$. Its finite filtrations and filtered comparison have underlying map $\sum_i H^0(RF(u_i))$, with every graded map invertible. Finite-filtration induction proves this map bijective. The required Grothendieck and K-injective hypotheses were checked in step 1; the lemma includes empty families and degrees below the common lower bound.

For any $K$ with quasi-coherent cohomology, put $A=\tau_{\leq -N-1}K$ and $K'=\tau_{\geq -N}K$. Step 1 checks the product-preserving hypothesis of the derived upper-bound lemma, and step 2 checks its uniform vanishing hypothesis. Apply it with $b=-N-1$ to $A$. It gives $H^m(RF(A))=0$ for $m\geq-1$, in particular for $m=0,1$. Apply the triangulated functor $RF$ to $A\to K\to K'\to A[1]$. In the long exact sequence, the terms adjacent to $H^0(RF(K))\to H^0(RF(K'))$ vanish, so this map is an isomorphism. The truncation maps are natural, making these isomorphisms natural in $K$. This is the single cutoff needed for all $E_i$ and their sum.

source.place: Tag 08F7, lemma-application-nice-K-injective; Tag 08FB, removal of the negative tail

proof.text: Apply step 5 to each $E_i$ and to $E$. Taking the direct sum of the former isomorphisms gives the left vertical isomorphism in the square comparing the original canonical map with the canonical map for $(\tau_{\geq-N}E_i)_i$. The right vertical map is the isomorphism for $E$. Step 1 identifies $\tau_{\geq-N}E$ with the coproduct of this truncated family. Each truncated object has the common lower bound $-N$, so step 4 makes the bottom comparison bijective. The square commutes on every summand by naturality of $K\to\tau_{\geq-N}K$; the coproduct universal property makes the whole square commute. Its top comparison is thus bijective. By definition it restricts to $H^0(X,\iota_i)$ on summand $i$, so it is the requested map. If $I$ is empty, the ambient coproduct is zero and the additive functor $H^0RF$ sends it to zero, giving the same conclusion.
